title: Sitharaman Pitches India as Defence and Tourism Hub in Chicago Meetings With US CEOs
excerpt: The finance minister met executives from Hyatt, Shield AI, and ADM during a nine-day Canada-US visit that includes the G20 Finance Ministers meeting.
body:
• Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman met executives from Hyatt, Shield AI, and ADM in Chicago on August 30, pitching India as an investment destination across defence, tourism, and agriculture
  • She addressed the Indian diaspora at the Consulate General, lauding their role in strengthening India's soft power and bilateral ties with the US
  • Sitharaman highlighted Tier-II and Tier-III cities as emerging economic hubs and proposed GIFT City as a financing center for multinational operations
  • The engagements are part of a nine-day joint Canada-US visit that includes the G20 Finance Ministers meeting in Asheville, North Carolina

Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held a series of high-level meetings with senior executives of major American corporations in Chicago on August 30, pitching India as a prime destination for investment in defence technology, hospitality, and agriculture, according to an official Finance Ministry statement.

The meetings came during a nine-day joint visit to Canada and the United States. Sitharaman arrived at Chicago's O'Hare International Airport on Thursday following a three-day visit to Canada for the inaugural India-Canada Economic and Financial Dialogue. She was welcomed by the Indian Embassy's Deputy Chief of Mission Namgya C. Khampa and the Consul General of India in Chicago, Somnath Ghosh.

Diaspora Outreach in Chicago

Sitharaman addressed the Indian diaspora community at the Consulate General of India in Chicago, calling them "a formidable force" that enhances India's soft power, global standing, and bilateral relationships with the United States, according to a Finance Ministry post on X. She emphasized India's potential as a global hub for developing, testing, and manufacturing autonomous defence systems, citing the country's technology capabilities, skilled workforce, and growing innovation ecosystem.

Defence Technology Ties With Shield AI

In a meeting with Brandon Tseng, co-founder and president of Shield AI, Sitharaman explored cooperation in AI-enabled autonomy, unmanned systems, and next-generation defence technologies. Discussions covered research and development, co-development, and co-production arrangements, according to the Finance Ministry statement.

"India's rapidly expanding defence technology ecosystem, strong engineering and AI talent, and growing capabilities in advanced manufacturing make it a natural partner for next-generation defence cooperation."

— Indian Finance Ministry statement

Tourism Push With Hyatt

Sitharaman met Mark S. Hoplamazian, president and CEO of Hyatt, to discuss the hotel chain's expansion in India. She pointed to opportunities in destination-led tourism spanning spiritual, cultural, wellness, medical, nature, and experiential segments, and encouraged Hyatt to leverage its asset-light model to deepen partnerships with Indian developers and investors, according to the Finance Ministry.

The minister highlighted India's improving connectivity and infrastructure, noting that Tier-II and Tier-III cities are emerging as important centers of economic activity and travel. She also proposed GIFT City as a potential financing and treasury hub for Hyatt's India operations and suggested exploring talent development through the National Institute of Hospitality.

Agriculture Expansion With ADM

With Monish Patolawala, executive vice president and CFO of agricultural giant ADM, Sitharaman discussed the company's presence in India and opportunities across agriculture, food, nutrition, technology, and sustainable value chains. She welcomed ADM's farmer partnerships, engagement with Farmer Producer Organisations, and its global technology and AI capabilities center in Bengaluru.

What's Next

Sitharaman will lead India's delegation at the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors meetings in Asheville, North Carolina, being held under the US presidency. The visit is scheduled to conclude on September 2. The Chicago engagements reflect a broader push by the Finance Ministry to position India as a multi-sector investment destination, with GIFT City and smaller cities featuring prominently in outreach to multinational corporations.
